one_line_contribution: A controlled attribution study claiming that the cost of a multi-writer agent skill library is not its size but the presence of precondition-overlapping skills from different writers that get co-retrieved and prescribe divergent action macros, plus a head-to-head governance comparison arguing that only query-time (activation-time) conflict handling survives a long stream with a mid-stream task-mix shift.
closest_prior_work: SkillAligner (arXiv:2608.06880, 2026-08-07, VERIFIED via the literature command on both s2 and hf channels): a training-free execution-time skill adaptation framework that treats retrieved skills as adaptable drafts, explicitly 'resolves conflicts' among retrieved procedural skills at execution time, reduces skill-induced regressions at the instance level, and lowers inference cost. That is the proposal's second headline clause -- activation-time reconciliation beats leaving retrieved skills as fixed instructions -- already demonstrated, and the proposal neither cites it nor surfaced it in its own collision check. It does not threaten the first half (writer-heterogeneity at matched size/coverage as the causal variable, conflict incidence as the mediator, k=1 falsification), which remains open. Two further verified neighbours crowd the harm-decomposition half: The Regression Tax (arXiv:2607.22520, 2026-07-24), which decomposes why procedural skills help and hurt into context effects, input misinterpretation and suppressed verification; and Right Family, Wrong Skill / SameCapRisk-Bench (arXiv:2606.10388, 2026-08-20), which measures exposure to same-capability-family sibling skills inside a retrieval set and shows clustering/controlled scoring mitigates it -- i.e. co-retrieval of near-duplicate-precondition skills is already an object of measurement, just not indexed by writer identity. On the writer axis, Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment (arXiv:2605.30723) and From Raw Experience to Skill Consumption (arXiv:2605.23899) already vary the authoring/consuming model, so 'who wrote the skill matters' is not itself new; what is new is holding size, coverage and tokens fixed while varying the number of distinct writers.
strongest_objection: The headline policy result is close to entailed by the proposal's own definitions, and confounded with injection volume -- the one lever this program has already shown to be causal. Conflict is defined as a query-conditioned event (two skills in the same top-k whose macros diverge). Write-time policies (usage pruning, keep-newest, verifier replay, LLM merge, random pruning) structurally cannot observe that event; only the activation-time policies can. So 'only activation-time reconciliation keeps its edge' is a restatement of the conflict definition, not a discovery. Worse, activation-time abstain removes an injected skill, so it reduces injected item count and tokens relative to every competitor, and the brief's own pilot reports that cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated memory harm outright. The same confound sinks Prediction (3): k=3 to k=1 cuts injected tokens roughly threefold, so a >=60% shrinkage of the heterogeneous penalty is the predicted consequence of dose reduction alone and cannot discriminate co-retrieval conflict from load. Second confound: the conflict-removed arm dedupes precondition clusters and tops up from the same contributors at matched N, which necessarily widens the precondition coverage of that arm -- so Prediction (2)'s 70% recovery is attributable to reduced redundancy/broadened coverage, not to conflict removal, and the 'coverage reduced, conflicts kept' arm moves a different axis in a different direction rather than restoring the match. Third: the central contrast is heterogeneous-mixed minus *best*-single, a maximum over four noisy single-contributor arms, which is upward-biased by selection and therefore biased toward the hypothesis; the noise band is then defined by re-running that same selected arm. Fourth: everything upstream rests on a detector -- exact first-divergent-action alignment on macros -- that is validated only by 'a local judge for label sanity' on 200 pairs with no pre-registered precision/recall threshold. In ALFWorld that detector will fire on any two skills for different task families (heat vs cool diverge at action one), inflating incidence and rendering the pre-registered >=10% gate vacuous, while missing the real disagreements, which are receptacle-choice and ordering variants that exact alignment treats as different sequences anyway. Fifth: Prediction (4) (usage-utility Spearman rho < 0.2) cannot fail -- attenuation from measurement error in a leave-one-skill-out utility estimated on a 300-task subsample will drive rho below 0.2 whether or not conflict is the cause, so the prediction is satisfied for the wrong reason and adds nothing causal to SkillFlow's published usage != utility finding.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a volume-matched abstention placebo: when the activation-time policy drops a skill from a conflicting pair, a control arm drops one skill at random from a matched non-conflicting retrieval, so item count and injected tokens are identical and the only difference is whether the dropped item was a conflict partner. Run the k ablation token-matched too, padding k=1 with the length-matched decoys already in the ablation list, so the k=1 prediction tests co-retrieval rather than dose. (2) Pre-register a detector quality gate, not a sanity check: report precision and recall of the alignment detector against a blind human/judge-labelled set of at least 300 co-retrieved pairs, with a minimum precision (e.g. 0.8) below which the mechanism claim is withdrawn; restrict conflict labels to pairs whose preconditions are matched, or the incidence gate is meaningless. (3) Replace best-single with a pre-registered comparator -- the mean of the four single-contributor arms, or a single contributor fixed in advance -- and derive the noise band from a held-out arm, to remove the max-selection bias. (4) Make the conflict-removal arm coverage-identical by construction: remove one member of each conflicting pair and top up with a skill drawn from the *same* precondition cluster from the same contributor, so the coverage histogram is unchanged and only conflict is removed. (5) State how leave-one-skill-out utility is estimated within budget (importance-weighted reuse of logged episodes, or restriction to episodes where the skill was actually retrieved), with the episode count, or drop it. (6) Cite and reimplement SkillAligner (2608.06880) as the activation-time arm rather than inventing abstain/likelihood-tie-break de novo, and reframe the contribution as the writer-heterogeneity attribution -- which is genuinely open -- rather than as 'only activation-time survives'.
missing_baseline: A token- and item-count-matched abstention placebo (drop a random skill from a matched non-conflicting retrieval set), which is the only way to separate 'conflict handling' from 'injecting less' given this program's own finding that injection volume was the causal lever. Secondarily: SkillAligner-style execution-time skill rewriting (2608.06880) as a published activation-time comparator, and a heterogeneous-mixed library whose contributors are matched on solo utility, to separate writer heterogeneity from writer quality spread.

Judging the proposal's own check: it is unusually transparent about its channel failures and did run both a recency-restricted mechanism query and a closest-method query, which is above average for this pool. But it ran essentially one mechanism query and one method query, and both missed 2608.06880, 2607.22520, 2606.10388, 2605.30723 and 2605.18401 -- five recent preprints that between them occupy the activation-time-reconciliation clause, the harm-decomposition framing, the co-retrieved-sibling measurement, the writer/consumer-model mismatch axis, and the library-governance-policy comparison. A check that reports eight Skill* hits and concludes 'no returned paper does X' without querying the read-time/execution-time reconciliation phrasing has under-searched exactly the half of its own title most likely to be scooped. ID verification: I verified 2604.17308 (SkillFlow), 2604.08377 (SkillClaw), 2605.09341 (SkillMAS), 2512.23760 (Audited Skill-Graph Self-Improvement -- returned not-found on first attempt, resolved on retry), 2605.12978 (Useful Memories Become Faulty), 2607.05844 (StateFuse), 2608.19701 (Beyond Memory Majority), 2606.24535 (Governed Shared Memory -- also not-found on first attempt, resolved on retry), 2607.10608 (The Compliance Trap), 2604.27003, 2608.11888, 2608.06880, and incidentally 2605.24117, 2605.18693, 2604.03088, 2604.20087, 2604.04323 via search hits. One mischaracterization: the proposal calls 2604.27003 'the stability-plasticity framing ... old-versus-new competition', but the verified record is 'When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents', a (k,v) study of representation and organization axes -- the citation should be checked. I did not attempt verification of 2606.03056 (SkillDAG), 2606.18051 (SkillWeaver), 2608.04828 (Skill-Use) or 2607.10113 (Dynamic Agent Skills survey), which appear only in the collision-check narrative and not in the novelty argument.
